newsitem.title: UK: Boots shrugs off hayfever drug withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Boots shrugs off hayfever drug withdrawal.

text.p: British pharmacist and high street retailer Boots Co Plc said on Friday that there would be little impact from the withdrawal of a hay fever treatment from over-the-counter sales.
"Basically, it's not an issue," a spokesman for the company said.
Boots said the total market for antihistamine treatments, which include those for hay fever was 38 million stg, and the company's share is around 35 percent.
Boots sales of Terfenadine, the withdrawn drug, amounted to 4.5 million stg a year, the spokesman said.
But he added that the drug would still be available on prescription and the company has its own-brand Cetirizine hay fever treatment as a direct replacement which is still available over-the-counter.
Boots shares had fallen on concerns over withdrawal of the drug, after the Health Department said on Thursday that 14 people had died since 1982 from taking Terfenadine.
The shares were down eight pence to 688.5 pence by 1145 GMT.
